instruction: DAE roundtrip fidelity. The input file `C:\Users\user\Desktop\orig.dae` is a COLLADA scene generated as if it had been exported from SketchUp. It contains: - 20 component instances (scene `<node>` elements that each carry one `<instance_geometry>`). - 5 shared `<geometry>` definitions in `<library_geometries>` (component instances re-use them, mimicking SketchUp's ComponentDefinition/ComponentInstance model): `geom-chair`, `geom-table`, `geom-shelf`, `geom-lamp`, `geom-bench`. - 3 `<material>` entries (`mat-wood`, `mat-metal`, `mat-fabric`) bound to different subsets of the 20 instances via the per-instance `<bind_material>` symbol `matref`. - 5 SketchUp-style tags ("layers") encoded inside group `<node>` `<extra>` blocks: `Structure`, `RoomA`, `RoomB`, `Fixtures`, `Misc`. - A 2-level nested group hierarchy: the scene root contains a `Floors` container, which contains `Floor_01` and `Floor_02` group nodes, each of which contains multiple `Room_*` group nodes, each of which contains the leaf component instance nodes. So the deepest named-node chain is `Floors > Floor_XX > Room_Y > Inst_ZZ` (depth 4). Your task mimics the SketchUp roundtrip test: export the scene to DAE, import that DAE back into a fresh empty scene, then re-export it a second time. Concretely: 1. Use `C:\Users\user\Desktop\orig.dae` as the initial scene. 2. Save it to an intermediate DAE (e.g. `tmp_a.dae`). 3. Load the intermediate DAE from disk and re-save it to `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae`. 4. Compare `C:\Users\user\Desktop\orig.dae` with `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae` and write `C:\Users\user\Desktop\report.json` with EXACTLY these four keys: ``` { "vertex_count_preserved": <bool>, // total vertex entries in <geometry>/<float_array> is identical "material_count_preserved": <bool>, // number of <material> entries is identical "hierarchy_depth_preserved": <bool>, // deepest named-node chain depth is identical "total_instances": <int> // count of scene <node>s carrying an <instance_geometry> in C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae } ``` The three booleans MUST be computed from actually measuring both DAEs - do not hardcode `true`. `total_instances` is an integer count measured on `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae`. Requirements: 1. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae` exists and parses via `pycollada`. 2. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\report.json` exists, is valid JSON, and has exactly the four keys above with the correct types (3 booleans + 1 integer). 3. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae` has the same total `<geometry>` vertex count as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\orig.dae`. 4. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae` has the same number of `<material>` entries as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\orig.dae`. 5. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae`'s scene-graph depth (deepest named-node chain) equals `C:\Users\user\Desktop\orig.dae`'s. 6. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae` carries exactly 20 instance nodes (scene `<node>`s with at least one `<instance_geometry>`). 7. The three `*_preserved` flags in `C:\Users\user\Desktop\report.json` equal the actual comparison between the input and output files; `total_instances` equals the actual instance count in `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae`. [Software] Launch SketchUp with `C:\SketchUp 2026 26.0.429 x64 En Portable\SketchUp.exe` (adjust if your install differs).
